land.text: Macedon, Thessaly and the Greek garrisons of Cassander's house, taken by Demetrius Poliorcetes when he 'established himself on the throne of Macedonia by murdering Alexander V' in 294 BC

successors.note: Cliopatria ends the row in -292 and starts 'Antigonid Dynasty' in -291; the Demetrius I page dates the seizure of the throne to 294 BC. The Antigonid rows are one state in polities/antigonid-dynasty.json.

land.text: Antigonus's kingdom of Asia (Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia, northern Mesopotamia and Cyprus), which left the nominal empire when he 'assumed the title of king' in 306 BC

successors.note: A split event in 306; the Antigonid dossier carries the Asian kingdom from 306 to Ipsus (301).

land.text: Babylonia (secured by Seleucus after Gaza, 312) and the upper satrapies to Bactria and the Indus after the Babylonian War (311-309)
Egypt and Libya, Ptolemy's satrapy, independent in fact from the death of Perdiccas (321) and confirmed to him at Triparadisus
Thrace, assigned to Lysimachus in 323 and his kingdom from 306/305
the Indus satrapies of Alexander (Gandhara and the Punjab), taken by Chandragupta c. 317 ('Jansari dates the arrival of Chandragupta in the Punjab at c. 317') from the Greek-Indian governors

successors.note: A loss event in 317; the Seleucid-Mauryan settlement of 305-303 (Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae) passed from the Seleucid Empire, not from this state.

capitals.name: Aigai (Vergina)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Aigai before 399 BC'. Royal burials stayed at Aigai after the move.

capitals.name: Pella
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Pella 399-168 BC'; Archelaus (413-399) moved the capital. Cassander died at Pella in 297.

rulers.name: Perdiccas I
rulers.note: Traditional founder, 'fl. c. 650 BC'; the early Argead dates are estimates and the kings before Amyntas I (Argaeus I fl. c. 623, Philip I fl. c. 593, Aeropus I fl. c. 563, Alcetas fl. c. 533) are placed here by their floruit only.

rulers.name: Amyntas I
rulers.note: c. 512 - 498/7; 'first king with reliable historical information'; Persian vassal.

rulers.name: Orestes
rulers.note: Minority reign under his guardian Aeropus II.

rulers.name: Amyntas II and Pausanias
rulers.note: Several months each, probably ruling alongside each other.

rulers.name: Amyntas III
rulers.note: Two reigns (393, then 393-369); Argaeus II was a pretender installed by the Illyrians.

rulers.name: Ptolemy of Aloros
rulers.title: Regent for Perdiccas III, or king (disputed)

rulers.name: Philip II
rulers.note: 360/59-336; regent for Amyntas IV at first, then king.

rulers.name: Philip III Arrhidaeus and Alexander IV
rulers.title: Joint kings under regents
rulers.note: Philip III 323-317, Alexander IV 323-310; regents Perdiccas (323-320), Peithon and Arrhidaeus (320), Antipater (320-319), Polyperchon (319-317), then Cassander. Alexander IV and Roxana were poisoned 'in either 310 BC or the following year' (Cassander page).

rulers.name: Cassander
rulers.title: Regent 317-305, king from 305
rulers.note: The king list gives 310-297; the Cassander page: regent from 317, 'he proclaimed himself king in 305 BC', died at Pella in 297. Antipatrid dynasty.

rulers.name: Antipater I and Alexander V
rulers.note: Co-rulers; Alexander V murdered by Demetrius Poliorcetes in 294, which ends this dossier.

Thessaly, whose league elected Philip archon in 352, is a ledger gain (352) and part of the state from then on; Olynthus and the Chalcidice (348) and Thrace to Philippopolis (342) are ledger gains inside this span.

218,219 km2 for 337-334, bbox 19.8-29.0 E and 39.0-45.0 N: Macedon, Thessaly and Thrace to the Danube. Philip's Thracian campaigns reached Philippopolis (342) and the sieges of Perinthus and Byzantium (340-339) failed; Alexander's 335 campaign 'reaches the Danube'. The Greek cities of the League of Corinth (337) are hegemony, not territory: correctly outside the shape.

584,874 km2 for 333-332, bbox to 36.8 E and 33.5 N: the Balkans, Asia Minor (Granicus May 334, Sardis, Halicarnassus 334, Cappadocia crossed 333) and, after Issus (November 333), Cilicia, Syria and Phoenicia (Tyre January-July 332, Gaza October 332). Egypt, entered after Gaza, is a ledger gain in late 332 and enters Cliopatria only through the mislabelled Ptolemaic shape of 331.

correction.text: the Balkan homeland (this shape), Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and Egypt (which Cliopatria carries in its 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' shape of 331-327, 1.22 M km2, a mislabelled row), and Babylonia and Susiana after Gaugamela (1 October 331: 'He then advances to Babylon and Susa'); the ledger adds Persis and Media (330), the eastern satrapies (330) and Bactria-Sogdia (329-327)

minus.text: Gedrosia (Makran) with Pakistani Baluchistan and Iranian Sistan-Baluchestan, the land of the return march of 325-324, without the Achaemenid satrapies of 331 (Carmania, Drangiana), which this state already holds as the Achaemenid successor of 330

This river thus marks the easternmost extent of his conquests'; 'led the rest back to Persia through the more difficult southern route along the Gedrosian Desert and Makran'; 'Alexander reached Susa in 324 BC'. correction.text: the whole empire 'from the Balkans and Egypt in the west to Central Asia and India in the east', which Cliopatria's 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' shape of 326-324 (4.83 M km2, Iran-centred) carries under the wrong name; with Sogdia, Bactria, Mesopotamia and the Punjab as the ledger gains of 331-326 hold them (Cliopatria's shape lacks about 560 Sogdian, 230 Bactrian, 720 Mesopotamian and 470 Punjab cells)

region.text: the Argead core around Aigai (Vergina) and the lower Haliacmon

ledger.note: c. 675: the Argead kingdom at Aigai. Cliopatria's first year; the page gives only a 'legendary foundation in the 7th century BC' by Perdiccas I or Caranus, and the king list 'fl. c. 650 BC' for Perdiccas I.

region.text: the Argead kingdom of Alexander I's predecessors, Lower Macedonia, made a Persian vassal under Darius I

ledger.note: 512/511: Macedon a vassal of Persia. Infobox: 'Vassal of Persia: 512/511-493 BC' and 'Incorporated into the Persian Empire: 492-479 BC'; the Alexander I of Macedon page: 'In 492 BC it was made a fully subordinate part of the Persian Empire by Mardonius' campaign'. The vassal relation belongs in both ledgers (achaemenid-empire carries the other side) and keyframes 1-3 rely on it. The first year is the infobox's 512 (or 511).

region.text: the Argead kingdom, free of Persian control after the Persian withdrawal

ledger.note: 479: Persian control over Macedon ends. Infobox 'Incorporated into the Persian Empire: 492-479 BC', 'marking the end of Persian control over Macedonia'; Alexander I had supplied troops to Xerxes I in 480-479.
399: the capital moves from Aigai to Pella. Archelaus (413-399) 'moved the capital to Pella'; the infobox dates Pella from 399 BC.

region.text: 'some territory' of Macedon given to Olynthos in 393/2; the page gives no extent, so a 25 km disc round Thessaloniki (the Thermaic coast beside the Chalcidice), as in the chalcidian-league dossier

ledger.note: 393/2: Amyntas III cedes land to Olynthos. 'In 393/2 BCE, Amyntas III of Macedon temporarily transferred some territory to Olynthos' (Chalcidian League page). Mirrors chalcidian-league's 393 gain; the extent is a reading.

region.text: the land transferred in 393/2, 'restored when Amyntas regained power'

ledger.note: 391: the land returns. 'It was restored when Amyntas regained power' (Chalcidian League page, no year; 391 follows the chalcidian-league dossier's reading of the Amyntas III page). Confidence 1: the page is silent on the year.

region.text: Pella, the Macedonian capital, held by the League after the second transfer 'to the entire League'

ledger.note: 385: Amyntas III cedes land, Pella included, to the whole League. 'Eight years later, Amyntas, who was again in trouble, handed over territory, this time to the entire League', which 'now included Pella, the Macedonian capital' (Chalcidian League page; 393/2 plus eight years, the page gives no calendar year). Mirrors chalcidian-league's 385 gain.

region.text: Pella, back from the dissolved League

ledger.note: 379: the League is dissolved and Pella returns. 'the Macedonians forced Olynthos to surrender and dissolve their Chalcidian League in 379 BC' (Macedonia page, after Olynthos had 'nearly overthrown' Amyntas III); 'in 379 BCE the cities of the former League became "autonomous"' (Chalcidian League page). Neither page says that Pella returned, which follows from the dissolution; mirrors chalcidian-league's 379 loss.

region.text: Amphipolis on the Strymon and Pydna on the Thermaic Gulf

ledger.note: 357: Amphipolis and Pydna taken. Philip 'Besieged and took Amphipolis, then captured and kept Pydna (the page dates both to 357 BC)'. Both were Greek cities, Pydna claimed by Athens.

region.text: Paeonia proper: the Axios (Vardar) valley from Demir Kapija north to the Skopje basin and the Strumica and Strymon uplands (Natural Earth North Macedonia and Blagoevgrad cut by a six-point polygon that leaves out Pelagonia, Lyncestis and the Ohrid lands, which are Upper Macedonian). kingdom-of-paeonia draws the whole country plus Blagoevgrad and should narrow to the same.

ledger.note: 356: Paeonia becomes subject to Philip II. 'In 356 BC, the Paeonian king Lyppeius became a subject to Philip II' (Paeonia page, which also has Philip's 'campaign deep into the north, into Paeonia itself' in 358). The Philip II page's 'Defeated the Paeonians, who were made to swear allegiance to Macedon' is that 358 campaign; the dossier now takes the Paeonia page's 356 for the subjection so that it agrees with kingdom-of-paeonia. The region is narrowed to Paeonia proper (see the text) because the whole of North Macedonia also holds Upper Macedonian Lyncestis and Pelagonia.

region.text: Crenides, refounded as Philippi, with the Pangaion mines

ledger.note: 356: Crenides becomes Philippi. 'Conquered Crenides and renamed it Philippi.' Potidaea, taken the same year, was 'Ceded to the Chalcidian League, as promised'.

region.text: Methone, 'the last Athenian-held city on the Thermaic Gulf'

ledger.note: 354: Methone falls; Philip loses an eye in the siege.

region.text: Thessaly, whose league elected Philip archon after Crocus Field and which the thessalian-league dossier closes with this state as successor

ledger.note: 352: Thessaly passes to Philip. 'Philip II in turn defeated Onomarchus in 352 BC at the Battle of Crocus Field, which led to Philip II's election as leader (archon) of the Thessalian League' (Macedonia page); 'He became archon of the Thessalian League' (Philip II page). Read as annexation rather than a vassal tint, because the thessalian-league dossier ends the League c. 353 with macedonian-empire as successor and the 350 Cliopatria shape already reaches Thessaly; the earlier vassal_start for a 'Thessalian League' had no living dossier behind it. Macedon holds Thessaly to 196 (antigonid-dynasty). The one-year difference with thessalian-league (353) is that page's 'around 353 BCE'.

region.text: Olynthus and the cities of the Chalcidian League

ledger.note: 348: Olynthus razed. 'Took Olynthus and razed it. The Chalcidian League dissolved.' Cliopatria has no Chalcidian League row; the land is inside its Greek City-States shapes.

region.text: the Odrysian kingdom of Cersobleptes in the Hebrus valley

ledger.note: 347: Cersobleptes submits. Philip 'Forced the Thracian prince Cersobleptes to submit'. Cliopatria's Odrysian Kingdom row runs to 338.

region.text: Molossia, the heartland of the Molossian state around Ioannina

ledger.note: 343/2: Philip II makes Alexander king of Epirus. 'in 343/2 Philip dethroned Arybbas and made Alexander, still in his late 20s, king of Epirus' (Alexander I of Epirus page); the Macedonia page: Philip 'deposed Arybbas in Epirus in favour of his brother-in-law Alexander I'. A Macedonian client kingship read as a vassal (rule 4); the marriage alliance with Philip's daughter followed in 337/336. Mirrors kingdom-of-epirus.

region.text: the Odrysian interior, campaigned through in 342

ledger.note: 342: the Thracian interior passes from submission to direct rule (next event).

region.text: the Hebrus valley: 'founded Philippopolis (modern Plovdiv) on the site of Eumolpia'; the coastal Greek cities reduced 'as far as the Hebrus'

ledger.note: 342: Philippopolis founded; Thrace annexed. 'Campaigned against the Scythians and founded Philippopolis' (342); the Macedonia page: 'conquered a Thracian city and renamed it Philippopolis' (342). The sieges of Perinthus (340) and Byzantium (339) 'both failed', so the Propontis coast stays Greek.

region.text: the upper Tonzos valley around Kazanlak and Stara Zagora, the Odrysian rump left under a Macedonian strategos

ledger.note: 340: inland Thrace under a strategos. 'The three Odrysian kingdoms were eventually conquered by the rising kingdom of Macedon under Philip II in 340 BC' and 'inland Thrace was not transformed into a Macedonian province, but was put under the loose control of a Strategos' (Odrysian kingdom page, the second sentence undated). Mirrors odrysian-kingdom's 340 events; the extent of the rump is that dossier's reading.

region.text: Naupactus

ledger.note: 338: Naupactus held by Philip before he gives it away. The Naupactus page says it 'passed into the hands of the Achaeans, from whom, however, it was wrested by Epaminondas', that 'the Locrians regained possession of the town' (undated) and that 'Philip II of Macedon gave it to the Aetolians'; no page opened says from whom Philip took it, so the counterpart is the catch-all greek-city-states and the confidence is 1.

region.text: Naupactus

ledger.note: 338: Philip gives Naupactus to the Aetolians. The Aetolian League page: the league gained 'Naupactus from Philip II of Macedon in 338 BC'; Naupactus page: 'Philip II of Macedon gave it to the Aetolians'. Mirrors aetolian-league's 338 gain.

region.text: the Greek states of the League of Corinth (Sparta excepted), of which Philip was elected hegemon

ledger.note: 337: the League of Corinth. After Chaeronea (338) Philip 'Was recognized as military leader of the League of Corinth, a Greek confederation against the Persian Empire' (338/7; the infobox gives 337). Hegemony, drawn as the lighter tint (rule 4), not as territory.

region.text: Thrace to the Danube: the Triballi and the Thracian tribes defeated in spring 335

ledger.note: 335: Alexander reaches the Danube. 'He campaigns in Thrace against the Illyrians and Triballi, reaches the Danube, and defeats Cleitus and Glaukias. While he is north, Thebes revolts and is razed to the ground.' Cliopatria's 337 shape already reaches 45 N.

region.text: western Asia Minor: Sardis and Halicarnassus (334), then Lycia, Pamphylia and Phrygia on the road to Gordium

ledger.note: May 334: the Granicus. 'After crossing the Hellespont, he wins the Battle of the Granicus. The satrap at Sardis is among the first to capitulate. Halicarnassus is besieged and taken in 334.' Lycia, Pamphylia and Gordium are not named on the page (the region list is the researcher's reading of the 333 march 'east through Cappadocia'). [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Sardis, Halicarnassus, Caria and Phrygia but not the Troad, Mysia, Ionia, Lycia or Pamphylia.]

region.text: Cappadocia, crossed on the march, and Cilicia beyond the Taurus, where Issus was fought

ledger.note: November 333: Issus. 'Before Issus, he marches east through Cappadocia and crosses Mount Taurus'; the battle is dated 'November 333 BC' (text) or '5 November 333 BC' (table).

region.text: Syria and Phoenicia; Tyre taken after a seven-month siege

ledger.note: January-July 332: the siege of Tyre. 'Tyre is besieged and captured.'

region.text: Gaza, which 'falls after three assaults' in October 332, and Egypt, entered after Gaza, 'where he is crowned and plans Alexandria'

ledger.note: October 332: Gaza falls; Egypt submits. The page gives no exact date for Egypt or Alexandria (331); the month is Gaza's. Cyrenaica's submission is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Molossia

ledger.note: 331: Alexander of Epirus dies. He 'was killed by a Lucanian' at the Battle of Pandosia (331 BC, Italy). The page says nothing of Epirus's relation to Macedon afterwards, so the end of the client kingship is bridged at his death (confidence 1); mirrors kingdom-of-epirus.

region.text: Megalopolis in Arcadia, besieged by Agis III

ledger.note: 331: Agis III's war. 'Two years after this Spartan success (331 BC), the Greek states which were in league against Alexander seized the opportunity to declare war against Macedonia'; 'Agis laid siege to Megalopolis. The city held out until Antipater came to its relief.' Mirrors peloponnesian-league's 331 contest.

region.text: Megalopolis

ledger.note: 331: Antipater's victory. Agis' army 'fought a larger Macedonian force, but was finally defeated at the Battle of Megalopolis in 331 BC, where he died'. No land changes hands.

region.text: Mesopotamia, Babylon and Susa after Gaugamela

ledger.note: 1 October 331: Gaugamela. 'He wins the Battle of Gaugamela. He then advances to Babylon and Susa.'

region.text: Persis (Persepolis 'looted and burned', winter 330) and Media (Ecbatana; Darius 'fatally stabbed by Bessus')

ledger.note: 330: Persepolis and the death of Darius. 'He forces the Persian Gate pass, then takes Persepolis, which is looted and burned'; Darius 'is fatally stabbed by Bessus' (330, no date on the page). Cliopatria's Achaemenid row keeps 3.5 M km2 to 327.

region.text: Hyrcania, Parthia, Aria, Drangiana and Arachosia, crossed on the pursuit of Bessus to Bactria

ledger.note: 330: the eastern satrapies on the road to Bactria. The page 'does not mention Ecbatana, Hyrcania, Aria, Drangiana, or Arachosia'; the year is bridged from the 329 Bactrian campaign that follows. A gap-filler should open 'Alexander the Great' or the satrapy pages.

region.text: Bactria and Sogdia: Cyropolis, the Jaxartes (October 329), the Sogdian Rock (327)

ledger.note: 329-327: Bactria and Sogdia. 'He campaigns in Bactria and Sogdia, takes Cyropolis, and wins at the Jaxartes (October 329). He takes the Sogdian Rock in 327.' The counterpart is Bessus's and Spitamenes's Persian successor regime.

intersect.text: the Achaemenid 331 shape inside Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan: the land achaemenid-empire ledger 44 split to Bessus in 330
the -326 keyframe of this dossier (its Gedrosia cut does not reach the split land)

minus.text: Bactria and Sogdia (the gain above) and Gandhara and the Punjab (the gains of 326)

region.text: Bessus's eastern realm outside Bactria and Sogdia (Aria, Drangiana, Arachosia and the Hindu Kush, Margiana and the Kopet Dag edge of Turkmenistan), as far as the -326 shape draws it; Gandhara and the Punjab stay with the 326 gains

ledger.note: 329: Bessus falls and the east he claimed passes to Alexander. Alexander page: 'In 329 BC, Spitamenes, who held an undefined position in the satrapy of Sogdiana, betrayed Bessus to Ptolemy, one of Alexander's trusted companions, and Bessus was executed' (the sentence is cut at 'betrayed Bessus to Ptolemy, one of Alexander's trusted companions, and Bessus was executed'); 'The campaign took Alexander through a number of satrapies in present-day Afghanistan and Central Asia' (Media, Parthia, Aria, Drangiana, Arachosia, Bactria, Scythia; no year), with 'Alexandria Arachosia at modern Kandahar'. The page dates no occupation of Aria, Drangiana or Arachosia, so the year is the fall of Bessus (bridged) and the region is the part of the land achaemenid-empire ledger 44 split to bessus-artaxerxes-v in 330 that the -326 keyframe draws as Alexander's, less Bactria and Sogdia (the gain above; they are all that bessus-artaxerxes-v passes on at its dissolve) and Gandhara and the Punjab (the gains of 326). Without it the rest of that land (about 2,400 cells: Hilmand, Hirat, Kandahar, Farah, Nimroz, Ghor, Chardzhou, Ahal, parts of K.P.) was nobody's from Bessus's dissolve and the -326 keyframe snapped it in. [fx-23 refix]

region.text: the Swat and Kabul valleys: Massaga, Ora and Aornos (April 326)

ledger.note: 327-326: the Assakenoi and Aspasioi. 'He campaigns against the Assakenoi and Aspasioi, taking Massaga, Ora, and Aornos (April 326).' Tribal land with no Cliopatria row ('nobody'); Taxiles's Taxila submitted.

region.text: the Punjab from the Hydaspes to the Hyphasis and down the Indus to the Malli at Multan

ledger.counterpart: Porus and the Indian kingdoms of the Punjab
ledger.note: May 326: the Hydaspes. 'He wins the Battle of the Hydaspes against Porus. His army then mutinies at the Hyphasis, which marks the eastern limit of his conquests'; 'He conquers the Malli at Multan' (326/325). Porus kept his kingdom as a client (rule 4 tint).

region.text: Gedrosia (Makran) and Carmania with Pakistani Baluchistan and Iranian Sistan-Baluchestan, the land of the return march of 325-324

ledger.note: 325: the return march through Gedrosia and Carmania. Alexander page: 'Alexander sent much of his army to Carmania (modern southern Iran) with general Craterus'; 'while he led the rest back to Persia through the more difficult southern route along the Gedrosian Desert and Makran'; 'Alexander reached Susa in 324 BC, but not before losing many men to the harsh desert'. The page dates the march by neither year, only India (326) before it and Susa (324) after it; -325 is the researcher's bridge (confidence 1). Before, the -326 keyframe (Cliopatria's 326-324 shape) drew these lands a year or two early.

region.text: the upper Tonzos valley around Kazanlak and Stara Zagora

ledger.note: c. 325: Seuthes III revolts. 'Seuthes revolted against Macedon in about 325 BC, after Alexander's governor' (Zopyrion) was beaten by the Getae (Seuthes III page); the Odrysian kingdom page has the rebellion 'at the end of the 330s or in the mid-320s (the dating is not entirely clear)'.

minus.text: Seuthes III's realm around Seuthopolis in the Kazanlak valley and the Stara Zagora plain — 'ruled only part of Thrace'
the upper Tonzos valley around Kazanlak and Stara Zagora — the tributary Odrysian rump under the Macedonian strategos

region.text: the Stara Zagora plain and the upper Tonzos beyond the Kazanlak valley

ledger.note: c. 325: Seuthes III's realm around Seuthopolis passes out of Macedonian hands. Same region as odrysian-kingdom's c. 325 gain; Seuthes 'ruled only part of Thrace', the coast staying with the Macedonian strategoi (and later Lysimachus).

region.text: the Greek states that revolted on Alexander's death

ledger.note: 323: the Lamian War breaks the League of Corinth. 'Athens and allies revolted after Alexander's death'; Thessaly, Phocis and Locris 'joined the Hellenic League' (the coalition is the athenian-coalition dossier).

region.text: Thessaly and the pass at Lamia, where 'Antipater remained besieged in Lamia for most of the winter 323-322 BC'

ledger.note: 323-322: the Lamian War's fighting zone (rule 6 blend).

region.text: Thrace, assigned to Lysimachus

ledger.note: June 323: the Partition of Babylon. 'It was held at Babylon in June 323 BC'; Perdiccas regent for the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV; the satraps 'became satrapies divided between' the senior officers. Thrace to Lysimachus, drawn as the empire's tint until he 'assumed the royal title' in 306/305.

region.text: Syria, assigned to Laomedon

ledger.note: June 323: Syria to Laomedon (Partition of Babylon; confirmed at Triparadisus 321).

region.text: Babylonia, assigned to Archon under the regent Perdiccas (Cliopatria's 'Perdiccas' row)

ledger.note: June 323: Babylonia under the regent. The page gives Babylonia to Archon; Cliopatria labels the shape 'Perdiccas' (323-319), the regent who held the kings and the royal army there.

region.text: Egypt, assigned to Ptolemy ('Egypt and Libya' at Triparadisus)

ledger.note: June 323: Egypt to Ptolemy. Cliopatria's Ptolemaic row has no shape for 323-308; the Ptolemaic dossier should add keyframes from 323 (Egypt as satrapy) or 321 (independent in fact).

region.text: Thessaly, settled at Crannon

ledger.note: 6 August 322: Crannon. 'The final battle took place at Crannon on 6 August 322 BC'; the Athenian fleet had been beaten off Amorgos 'In the late summer 322 BC'; infobox 'Macedonian victory'.

region.text: Athens under the Munychia garrison and the oligarchy, and the Greek cities under Antipater's settlement

ledger.note: 18 September 322: the garrison enters Munychia. 'Antipater demanded the installation of a Macedonian garrison in the fortress of Munychia', taken 'on 18 September 322 BC'; 'only citizens with properties worth more than 2,000 drachmas retained their political rights'; Athens lost Oropus and Samos. The Aetolians 'escaped unscathed' and are not inside this tint.

region.text: Egypt and Libya, confirmed to Ptolemy at Triparadisus

ledger.note: 321: Ptolemy independent in fact. Perdiccas 'was assassinated after a failed Nile crossing' (Diadochi page) and at Triparadisus in 321 'Antipater was chosen to be a new regent' while Egypt and Libya went to Ptolemy; from here the ptolemaic-kingdom dossier draws Egypt in its own colour.

region.text: Babylonia, reassigned from the dead regent's party to Seleucus

ledger.note: 321: Babylonia to Seleucus at Triparadisus ('Babylonia: Seleucus'). Cliopatria keeps the Perdiccas row to 319 and starts the Seleucid row in 318.

region.text: Babylonia under Seleucus as satrap of the kings

ledger.note: 321-312: Seleucus's satrapy as the empire's tint. He fled to Ptolemy when Antigonus 'seized the treasuries at Susa and entered Babylon' after Gabiene (316/315) and 'secured Babylon' again after Gaza (312).

region.text: Egypt and Libya, Ptolemy's satrapy, which keyframes 13-14 take out of the empire's shape

ledger.note: 321: Egypt and Libya leave the empire. Triparadisus (321) left Ptolemy 'Egypt with Libya, and all the vast waste beyond it, and whatever else had been acquired to the westward'; the page does not say he became independent, which is the reading from the vassal_end above (Perdiccas's failed Nile crossing and death, 321). Backs the removal of the Nile Valley and Cyrenaica from the shapes of 321 on; the same pair as the Seleucid case in 312.

region.text: Syria, lost by Laomedon

ledger.note: 319: Laomedon's Syria ends (Cliopatria's year). The pages opened confirm Laomedon's satrapy in 323 and 321 but are silent on Ptolemy's seizure of Syria (usually 319/318); the Ptolemaic and Laomedon dossiers should settle it.

region.text: Macedon and Athens, fought over between Polyperchon (regent 319-317) with Olympias and Cassander

ledger.note: 317: Cassander against the regent. Cassander 'declared himself Regent in 317 BC' and 'put Athens under the control of Demetrius of Phaleron'; Polyperchon 'suffered a major setback at Megalopolis in 317 BC' and Olympias 'led an army into Macedon' (Polyperchon page). Cliopatria draws Polyperchon's Macedon as a row of its own (318-316).

region.text: the Indus satrapies of Alexander, Gandhara and the Punjab

ledger.note: c. 317: Gandhara and the Punjab pass to Chandragupta. 'Chandragupta attacked the Greek-Indian governors during a period of unrest and local warfare after Alexander's death'; 'Jansari dates the arrival of Chandragupta in the Punjab at c. 317, in line with the chronology of Greek history'; 'Peithon withdrew to Arachosia (Kandahar) in 316'. The war of 305-303 with Seleucus ended with a treaty by which he 'surrendered the easternmost parts of the provinces of Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae' (Seleucus I Nicator page): that cession is Seleucus's loss (seleucid-empire and maurya-empire dossiers), not this ledger's. Sindh and Balochistan are not named on the pages and stay in the shapes.

region.text: Macedon, secured by Cassander at Pydna

ledger.note: Spring 316: Pydna falls; Olympias killed. 'When the city fell in the spring of 316, Olympias was killed'; Cassander confined Alexander IV and Roxana at Amphipolis and founded Thessalonica and Cassandreia. Polyperchon was 'driven from Macedon by Cassander' and kept only Peloponnesian strongholds.

region.text: Macedon and Thessaly, the regent's government that Cassander overthrew

ledger.note: Spring 316: Cassander takes Macedon from the regent. 'When the city fell in the spring of 316, Olympias was killed'; Cassander 'further cemented his authority by founding Thessalonica, Cassandreia, and rebuilding Thebes' (316); the Polyperchon page: 'Shortly thereafter, Polyperchon was driven from Macedon by Cassander'. Mirrors polyperchon's 316 loss, whose region (Macedon and Thessaly) is used; Thessaly is not named on the Cassander page. Polyperchon's rebel hatch lies over this state's colour for 317-316 (the keyframes no longer subtract Cliopatria's Polyperchon row).

region.text: Paeonia proper: the Axios (Vardar) valley from Demir Kapija north to the Skopje basin and the Strumica and Strymon uplands (Natural Earth North Macedonia and Blagoevgrad cut by a six-point polygon that leaves out Pelagonia, Lyncestis and the Ohrid lands, which are Upper Macedonian). kingdom-of-paeonia draws the whole country plus Blagoevgrad and should narrow to the same.

ledger.note: 315: Paeonia independent again under Audoleon. The page lists Patraus (335-315) as 'a subject to Alexander the Great' and Audoleon (315-285) as one who 'became an independent king of Paeonia'; the year is the page's regnal date, the end of Macedonian overlordship is the researcher's reading (the page does not say what Cassander did in 315). Region narrowed to Paeonia proper as in the 356 event; the keyframes for 315-294 subtract it, so the independent Paeonian kingdom is not drawn in Macedon's colour.

region.text: Babylonia, where 'Seleucus secured Babylon' after Gaza

ledger.note: 312: Seleucus returns to Babylon as his own master.

region.text: Babylonia

ledger.note: 312: Babylonia lost to Seleucus. 'Ptolemy and Seleucus defeated Demetrius at Gaza (312), after which Seleucus secured Babylon.' The Seleucid era counts from 312/311; Cliopatria's Seleucid row has no shape until 307.

union.text: the upper satrapies from Susiana and Media to Bactria, held by Seleucus at the end of the Babylonian War

region.text: the upper satrapies from Susiana and Media to Bactria, held by Seleucus at the end of the Babylonian War, and the rest of the 315 shape east of Mesopotamia (Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan and the Central Asian and Indian corners the shape reaches)

ledger.note: 309: the east passes to Seleucus. The Babylonian War (311-309) was a 'Seleucid victory' (Diadochi page); 'a peace was concluded between Antigonus and Seleucus', leaving each in his realm, and Antigonus's 'empire and alliance system now comprised Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia'. The Punjab had already passed to Chandragupta (maurya-empire, Cliopatria row from 318), which no page opened dates. [fx-23] Widened to everything the -315 shape holds east of Mesopotamia: the named satrapies left about 5,600 cells (Baluchistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Badakhshan and others) in this state, so the -307 keyframe, which already excluded them, removed them as a snap. Wars of the Diadochi page: the Babylonian War 'was a conflict fought between 311 and 309 BC' and ended 'with Seleucus ruling the eastern provinces'; Antigonus page: Seleucus 'secured control over the eastern provinces'. (The Indus lands pass from Seleucus to Chandragupta c. 305-303 on other pages; not drawn here.)

region.text: the Peloponnese under Polyperchon as Cassander's strategos, 'nearly the entire peninsula, with the exceptions of Corinth, Sicyon, and Sparta' by 304

ledger.note: 309: Polyperchon becomes Cassander's man in the Peloponnese. After 'Polyperchon murdered the boy [Heracles] in 309 BC', Cassander 'agreed to formally recognize Polyperchon not only as strategos of the Peloponnese' and as a co-ruler.

region.text: Athens and the Greek cities, freed from Cassander's garrisons by Demetrius

ledger.note: 307: Antipater's settlement of Greece ends. 'Demetrius ousted Cassander's governor and took Munychia.'

region.text: Athens and Munychia

ledger.note: 307: Demetrius takes Athens. 'Demetrius ousted Cassander's governor and took Munychia' (307 BC).

region.text: Thrace, now Lysimachus's kingdom

ledger.note: 306/305: Lysimachus king. 'In 306/305 BC, Lysimachus followed the example of Antigonus and assumed the royal title.' The nominal empire of the kings had ended with Alexander IV's murder (310/309).

region.text: Antigonus's kingdom: 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia' and Cyprus, conquered in 306

ledger.note: 306: Antigonus king. After Salamis 'Antigonus assumed the title of king'; the Antigonid dynasty page's infobox 'Established: 306 BC'. From here the Asian kingdom is the antigonid-dynasty dossier's and Cassander's Macedon alone keeps this colour.

305: Cassander proclaims himself king; the Antipatrid dynasty replaces the Argeads on the same land (rule 2: same colour). 'he proclaimed himself king in 305 BC', having had 'Alexander IV and Roxana secretly poisoned in either 310 BC or the following year'.

region.text: Corinth and the Greek cities taken by Demetrius in 304-303 as 'liberator' of the revived Corinthian League

ledger.note: 304-303: Demetrius 'returned a second time to Greece as liberator, and reinstated the Corinthian League'; 'In 304-303 he seized cities including Corinth'. Polyperchon's Peloponnese shrank with it (next event).

region.text: the Peloponnese, where Polyperchon 'was left with only a few remaining cities, including Messenia and Mantineia'

ledger.note: 303: Polyperchon's Peloponnese falls to Demetrius; he is last heard of after 304.

region.text: Macedon, Thessaly and the Greek garrisons of the Antipatrids

ledger.note: 294: Demetrius Poliorcetes takes the throne of Macedon. 'In the same year he established himself on the throne of Macedonia by murdering Alexander V, the son of Cassander'; the Cassander page: Demetrius 'killed Alexander V and established the Antigonid dynasty'. Cliopatria keeps the row to 292 and starts the Antigonid row in 291.

wars.name: Philip II's wars of expansion (Third Sacred War and the northern conquests)
wars.outcome: Macedon takes the Thermaic and Strymon coasts, the Chalcidice and the Pangaion mines, becomes archon of Thessaly (352) and ends the Sacred War in 346 with the peace 'sworn in Thessaly'.
wars.note: The Paeonians (358) and Illyrians (Erigon Valley, 357; Pleuratus of the Ardiaei, 345) are the page's dated campaigns on the northern frontier; the zones listed are the ones that changed hands.

wars.name: Philip II's Thracian and Greek campaigns (Chaeronea)

zones.text: Chaeronea, 338: Thebes and Athens defeated; no land annexed

wars.outcome: Thrace to the Hebrus annexed (342); the sieges of Perinthus (340) and Byzantium (339) 'both failed'; Chaeronea (338) gives Macedon the hegemony of the League of Corinth (337), not Greek territory.

wars.name: Alexander's Balkan campaign
wars.outcome: The Triballi and the Illyrians defeated and the Danube reached; Thebes destroyed after its revolt. The Thracian frontier settles on the Danube.

wars.name: Wars of Alexander the Great
belligerents: Porus and the Indian kingdoms of the Punjab
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Macedonian victory': the Achaemenid Empire conquered; the Macedonian Empire 'spans from the Balkans and Egypt in the west to Central Asia and India in the east'. Alexander dies at Babylon in June 323.
wars.note: Dates on the page: Granicus May 334; Issus November 333; Tyre January-July 332; Gaza October 332; Gaugamela 1 October 331; Jaxartes October 329; Aornos April 326; Hydaspes May 326; the Malli November 326-February 325.

wars.name: Agis III's war

zones.text: the siege of Megalopolis and the battle, 331

wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: Antipater relieved Megalopolis and Agis III was killed in the battle; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Lamian War

zones.text: Athens, garrisoned at Munychia from 18 September 322

wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Crannon 6 August 322, the Athenian fleet beaten off Amorgos; Athens takes a garrison and an oligarchy and loses Oropus and Samos; the Aetolians 'escaped unscathed'.

wars.name: Wars of the Diadochi

zones.text: Antigonus against Eumenes 320-316; Lysimachus's invasion 302; Ipsus 301

wars.outcome: Infobox: First War (321-319) Antipatrid victory; Second (318-316) Antigonid-led coalition victory; Third (315-311) Antigonid defeat; Babylonian War (311-309) Seleucid victory; Fourth (307-301) Antigonid defeat. After Ipsus (301) 'The empire was carved up between the victors': Ptolemy keeps Egypt, Seleucus takes eastern Asia Minor (and Syria), Lysimachus 'the remainder of Asia Minor', Cassander Macedon.
wars.note: The page's own span is 322-272 BC; this dossier ends in 294. The contested zones drawn in the blend are only Macedon in 317-316 (ledger); the Asian fronts belong to the Antigonid, Seleucid and Ptolemaic dossiers.

certainty.note: Tribal and satrapal frontiers throughout: the Illyrian and Paeonian frontier in the north, the Thracian frontier on the Danube after 335, the satrapy boundaries of the Persian empire after 334 are all approximate. The Greek cities' territories are soft too; only the city perimeters are known.

notes:
Scope of this dossier: Cliopatria's 'Macedonian Empire' row (-675..-292) is read as the Kingdom of Macedon under the Argead and Antipatrid houses, including Alexander's empire and the nominal empire of the joint kings down to Antigonus's royal title (306), and ending when Demetrius Poliorcetes took the throne in 294 (Cliopatria -292). The Antigonid rows ('Antigonid Dynasty' -291..-278 and 'Antigonid Macedonia' -277..-165, one Wikidata id) are one state in polities/antigonid-dynasty.json. Both dossiers take the 'hellenistic' family; the reviewer may prefer to treat all three rows as one Kingdom of Macedonia under rule 2 (the Wikipedia article 'Macedonia (ancient kingdom)', Q83958, runs to 168 BC), in which case the Antigonid dossier's ledger merges into this one with a rename in 294 and Lysimachus's and Pyrrhus's years as losses.

Cliopatria rows to correct (all in keyframe_review): 331-324, when the Macedonian Empire shrinks to the Balkans while Alexander's conquests sit in the mislabelled 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' shapes (1.22 M km2 for 331-327, 4.83 M km2 for 326-324) and the Achaemenid row keeps 3.5 M km2 to 327; the overlap of the 323-319 shape with the Lysimachus, Laomedon and Perdiccas rows; the overlap of 318-316 with the Polyperchon row; the absence of any Seleucid shape for 316-308 and of any Ptolemaic shape for 323-308 (so Egypt and Babylonia-Iran are undrawn in those years unless those dossiers add keyframes); the 307-302 shape that fuses Cassander's Macedon with Antigonus's Asia; the 301-292 shape's reach to 34.3 E (Cilicia, Pleistarchus?), unconfirmed.

States Cliopatria lacks that this dossier's counterparts need: the Paeonian kingdom (vassal from 358 on the Philip II page, 356 on the Paeonia page, independent again from 315; its dossier kingdom-of-paeonia now exists and the counterpart is its slug), the Chalcidian League (to 348; dossier chalcidian-league now exists and the 348 gain names it), the Triballi, the Thessalian League (vassal from 352, inside Cliopatria's Greek City-States; a dossier thessalian-league exists but ends in 353 with Philip's takeover, so the counterpart here stays the name 'Thessalian League' and the reviewer should reconcile the two models), Eumenes's Cappadocia, Peithon's Media, Peucestas's Persis, Asander's Caria and the other Asian satrapies of 323-316 (the me-05 group's), Antigonus's kingdom 306-301 (written here into antigonid-dynasty as a new keyframe). Macedon under Ptolemy Keraunos, Meleager, Antipater Etesias and Sosthenes (281-277) has no Cliopatria shape and no dossier yet (see the notes file).

Disagreements between pages: Cassander's death 297 (Cassander page, king list) or 298 (Diadochi page); Pyrrhus expelled from Macedon 285 (Lysimachus page) or 284 (Pyrrhus page, Diadochi page, king list); Alexander IV's murder 310 or 309; Issus 'November 333' or '5 November 333'; Triparadisus 321 (Triparadisus page) against the common 320.

Pages that would help a gap-filler: 'Alexander the Great' (the 330 march through Hyrcania, Aria, Drangiana and Arachosia, which the campaigns page omits), 'Alexander I of Macedon' is silent on Bisaltia and Crestonia, 'Antipater' and 'Olympias' for 319-316, 'Pleistarchus' for Cilicia 301-299, 'Chandragupta Maurya' or 'Seleucus I Nicator' for the cession of the Indus satrapies (c. 305-303). The list-of-kings page 'List of ancient Macedonian kings' returned not found; 'List of kings of Macedonia' loaded.

Fix run of 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review). Changed: (1) keyframe 307-302 now keeps the Balkan part only (the shape is 1.53 M km2 to 75.5 E: it carried the Iranian plateau, Afghanistan, the Punjab and India's north-western corner); it also loses Athens from 307 and, in the new keyframe -304, Corinth, Boeotia and Euboea. (2) New ledger events: Persian vassalage 512-479 (achaemenid-empire); the Chalcidian League's hold on Thessaloniki (393-391) and Pella (385-379) with four new keyframes; the Epirote client kingship 343-331; the Thracian strategos 340 and Seuthes III's revolt c. 325; Naupactus 338 (gain from greek-city-states at confidence 1, loss to aetolian-league); Agis III's war 331 (event pair, war entry); Egypt and Libya out in 321 (ptolemaic-kingdom, new keyframe -321); Gandhara and the Punjab out c. 317 (maurya-empire, new keyframe -317); the 316 gain from polyperchon. (3) Thessaly is now a 352 gain from thessalian-league instead of a vassal of a league with no living dossier. (4) Paeonia: the subjection is dated 356 (Paeonia page) to agree with kingdom-of-paeonia, and the region is narrowed to Paeonia proper in the events and subtracted in the keyframes of 315-294; kingdom-of-paeonia should narrow its own region the same way (it draws all of North Macedonia plus Blagoevgrad, which holds Upper Macedonian Lyncestis and Pelagonia). (5) Keyframe 318 no longer subtracts Cliopatria's Polyperchon row. (6) The 34.3 E reach of the 301-292 shape is Cyprus (17 cells), not Cilicia; subtracted, because Demetrius held it to 295/294.
Disagreements kept: the first Thracian submission stays at 347 (Philip II page) whereas odrysian-kingdom has 352; the Odrysian kingdom page has Cersobleptes surrendering and giving a hostage in 351 and the front 'peaceful until 347 or early 346', so the three dossiers' dates are one to five years apart and the pages do not settle it. Counterparts to fix elsewhere: maurya-empire needs the c. 317 gain of Gandhara and the Punjab (sa-02); ptolemaic-kingdom needs the 321 gain of Egypt and Libya from this state and the 294 gain of Cyprus from antigonid-dynasty (me-05); kingdom-of-epirus 343/331 mirrors exist; the chalcidian-league mirrors for 391 (this state's gain) and 379 exist. [fx-23, 2026-11-01] Snaps of -326 and -307 repaired. -326: the keyframe no longer draws Gedrosia, Carmania, Pakistani Baluchistan and Iranian Sistan-Baluchestan before the new gain of -325 (return march, Alexander the Great page: India 326, Susa 324), and adds the Sogdia, Bactria, Mesopotamia and Punjab cells of the ledger; new keyframe -325. -307: the Asia exclusion moves from the -307 keyframe to a new -306 keyframe to agree with the -306 split (Antigonus king 306); the -309 loss to Seleucus covers the whole east of the 315 shape. Pages: Alexander the Great, Wars of the Diadochi, Antigonus I Monophthalmus.
